But there were liaisons in -- as far as I know, in Tuzla, and I am not -- I think also in Zenica, but I am not sure of that. So we passed our reports to Zenica, and if there were questions on that level with liaisons, that should be asking Tuzla or Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: Defence counsel showed you reports that you drafted in July and in August. I thought that the reports were drafted on a daily basis. Having read the documents, I noted that there are some days that are missing. In August, for example, the 5th, the 7th, the 9th of August, the 6th of August, the 8th of August, et cetera. Did you write reports every day? Does that mean that the Defence just selected certain reports, or were there days on which you did not write any reports?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: We had to write every day reports and we did. And the Defence just selected some days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that you were shown nine documents for July, ten for August, and -- for example, on the first list of documents, the 20th, the 21st, the 22nd, the 24th, and the 27th of July don't appear. But you wrote reports every day.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my last question: You were in a hierarchy when involved in this mission. You were part of a hierarchy. And this can be seen because your reports contain very specific paragraphs. You didn't decide to have such paragraphs. You have paragraphs concerning the general, political, and military situation. So this was established by someone else. These paragraphs were established by someone else and you were requested to provide information under these headings on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: We wrote and made statements about every paragraph and not someone else. Political is a bit difficult for us as a military officer. But it was at the end rather easier because sometimes it was a political question: What do you think? And we've got it from a higher level, then should we ask what the people on the ground were thinking about the defence armour plan or something. And we answered a question and then we got an answer and we wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were told by your superiors that there was a problem and that you should be told what you thought about the Vance-Owen Plan in the field, for example. That's what you're telling us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Just a few minor questions, Witness. You mentioned today that on a certain day the responsibility for the detainees was transferred from civil authorities to the military authorities, and you also mentioned that in your report of the 5th of August that has been shown to you. I wonder, was this an important event for you? Why did you mention it twice?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, at that moment it was not such an important event, but of course we were thinking why that happened. And until now I've got no answer about that. And first we were thinking that Senad Dautovic was moved away, but later on he was back again. And more we couldn't find out, so we had our questions. But we had no answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: It seemed in what you said in the foregoing - but I may be mistaken - that you thought Dautovic was deciding on the transfer. But I may be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: On which transfer? Dautovic had made a decision?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Yes. The decision to transfer was his.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, no, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: That was not -- no, that -- it must be from a higher level. But we do not know the reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: My main question is the following: You mentioned the fact that this had been done, and my question to you is: Did it have any consequences that you could observe yourself?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: After that, we -- as far as I can recall now, that after that day we didn't saw the prisoners any more. We didn't visit the POW cages. For instance, I didn't -- I'm sure of that -- the battalion commander any more. I asked specifically that I want to see them because at a certain time my opinion was that he was very frightened, the battalion commander, from the imprisoned battalion. But I never saw that guy, the battalion commander, any more. That's the only thing I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You just said after that day we didn't see the prisoners any more.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Not from the battalion, no. I think I only was at the stadium after the 5th, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: But had that any relation with the change, or was it just a coincidence?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I think that had relation. But the only thing I think, we couldn't investigate on that change and see everything we want. And there also was no POW exchange which was decided by a higher level, I heard just before. And -- well ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did it make your visiting the prisoners more difficult, or was there no difference in that respect?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: It was -- how do you call it -- postponed? Is postponed right answer? You get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I don't know. You tell me.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: No, "postponed," that is that the right word? We tried to make new visits to the POWs, and then they say, "Well, tomorrow or next week." Or "we have to discuss about that." Or "they are transferred to Zenica." And all these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So there were more delays.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: More delays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: More excuses.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, more excuses. That's a better word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: It didn't become possible at all.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: At the end I didn't see them any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And what is the end for you.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: The 12th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Then I was transferred to Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Benjamin, do you have any questions that arise from the questions the Judges have asked the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel? Do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. President, I have a number of questions. Further cross-examination by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lieutenant Colonel, the Judges asked you some questions about the decision you mentioned in the report dated the 5th of August, according to which responsibility for the prisoners would be transferred from the civilian police to the military authorities. Would it in fact be correct to say that up until that day there were a number of detention facilities in Bugojno? There was the furniture salon, the Gimnazija, the primary school, et cetera. And you visited these places having obtained permission to do so by the chief of the civilian police, Senad Dautovic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, the chief of the civilian police, who was accountable to the War Presidency in Bugojno as a civilian body, informed you that as of that day - and that was after the death of Mladen Havranek - he informed you that the responsibility that was -- the responsibilities of the civilian police would be transferred to the military authorities in Bugojno. Is that what was said? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be correct to say that you were told that the War Presidency would take a decision for the Iskra sports stadium to be transformed into a prison and you were told that other detention facilities would be closed down with the exception of the primary school? Is that what you were told?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they would be transferred to the sports stadium, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you also aware of the fact that the War Presidency in Bugojno decided that the stadium should be transformed into a detention facility and the prisoners of war previously detained in the furniture salon and in other facilities were transferred there? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I'll read first. I'm aware of the fact that the people should be transferred there. I can't confirm if everybody was transferred to the sports stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also told at that meeting that the civilian police would remain responsible for the facilities in which their colleagues, members of the HVO police, were detained? And this is something that you included in one of your reports too.

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I -- no. I can't recall that. No. It's not ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that after the Iskra Stadium had been set up - that is to say, several days after the meeting - you personally went to visit the Iskra Stadium? You saw that there were over 100 prisoners there and you recognised a commander among them, a commander from the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade whom you had seen before that date. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: I visited the stadium, the sports stadium. And as far as I can remember now, I didn't see the commander Eugen Kvaternik -- from the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I ask, are these -- is my friend's questions not arising from the questions that arose from the Bench or are we getting new -- another form of cross-examination? Because this doesn't seem to arise from the questions that were posed from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Residovic, the Judges didn't ask any questions about the Iskra Stadium. What are you getting at?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm just following up on your questions because you asked the witness whether the conditions changed and whether he was able to visit the detainees. After the meeting, the witness just confirmed that after the Iskra Stadium had been established he had no problems in visiting it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct? So after the BH army took over responsibility for these prisons, you were able to gain access to the Iskra Stadium; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: You were able to -- oh, I'll wait. Was I able to gain access? Yes, I've been there, in the sports stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you whether it would be correct to say that after this event, when you were informed that the military authorities would take over responsibility for the prisons? Would it be correct to say that on one occasion Father Janko told you that a group of unknown armed men broke into the stadium at night, they beat the detainees, and the guards didn't manage to prevent them to do this, although they tried to do so? Do you remember this event in August and do you remember including information on the event in your reports?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This information was handed over to us from Father Janko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question, Lieutenant Colonel: Could you confirm that Senad Dautovic, the chief of the civilian police, was in fact responsible to the War Presidency, the president of which was Mr. Mlaco, and other bodies -- you most frequently reported to the War Presidency, the president of the War Presidency in order to reach agreement on certain issues you were interested in?

utterances.speaker: RUDY GERRITSEN
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about aid, bringing in, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in view of the question raised about the documents we have presented, it's true that in accordance with the Rules of this Tribunal each party presents evidence that can support their case. Out of all the documents, out of all the daily reports, the Prosecution has only tendered the documents dated the 5th and 10th of August. The Defence has tendered a series of documents that demonstrate the numerous activities the witness was involved in, and this is the reason for which we have insisted on having access to all the archives, because it is clear to us that the party representing the Prosecution only looks for the documents they need when searching through thousands of documents. And likewise the Defence only tries to obtain the documents that are relevant to the Defence when going through the documents in question. I thought it was important to inform you of this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does the other Defence team have any cross-examination for the witness? We have very little time left now, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lieutenant Colonel, this completes your testimony. Thank you for having come and for having testified about the events you were familiar with in August 1993. We wish you all the best in your military career, and I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecution tell me about the schedule for tomorrow. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.00 p.m.,
